title: Attention Is All You Need
content: The 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need introduced the Transformer, an architecture that uses self-attention rather than recurrent layers to process sequences. Self-attention lets each token compare itself with other tokens, while positional information preserves sequence order. Multiple attention heads can learn different relationships in parallel. The encoder-decoder model achieved strong translation results and trained efficiently because sequence positions could be processed in parallel. Its ideas later became central to large language models, a reminder that a clear new perspective can reshape what a whole field is able to build.

title: The dishwasher peace treaty
content: We had both been loading the dishwasher with the quiet intensity of people who believe there is one correct geometry. We finally agreed that bowls go on the top rack and that neither of us is allowed to say "I told you so" until the cycle ends. The plates came out clean. Diplomacy remains a work in progress.

title: A very small mystery
content: The houseplant has a tiny paper hat. No one admits to making it. The plant seems pleased.

title: Birdwatching, technically
content: I bought a small notebook for birdwatching and went to the park with the confidence of someone who had read half an article. The first bird I saw was a pigeon. I wrote "pigeon, very sure of itself." After that, I noticed a blackbird, two sparrows arguing over a crumb, and a duck that looked as if it had somewhere important to be. I still cannot identify every bird, but I can now spend an hour outside without checking my phone. The notebook has become less of a field guide and more of a record of tiny neighborhood personalities.

title: The museum audio guide
content: I rented the museum audio guide and accidentally selected the children's tour. A cheerful voice explained the ancient vase as "a very old cup that had a big day." Honestly, that was enough context for me. I saw more exhibits than usual and learned that history is easier to remember when someone lets it be a little funny.

title: Pancakes for one, plus the optimistic extra
content: One egg, some flour, milk, and the confidence to make four pancakes instead of two.

title: The umbrella's big day
content: The forecast promised sun, so I left my umbrella at home. Naturally, it rained. I ducked into a bakery, where the person ahead of me was also waiting out the weather and offered to share the newspaper. We ended up comparing favorite soup recipes while the storm passed. By the time I stepped outside, the rain had stopped and I had a new recipe for lentil soup. The umbrella missed its outing, but the day managed to be useful anyway.

title: Minutes from the household meeting
content: Agenda: decide where the new lamp should go. Attendees: me, one cat. The cat sat in the box the lamp came in and declined to comment. After a long silence, I put the lamp by the chair. The cat approved by falling asleep under it. Motion carried.

title: A shortcut with a scenic detour
content: I tried a new shortcut home and got turned around near the community garden. A volunteer was watering the tomatoes and pointed me in the right direction, then insisted I take a handful of cherry tomatoes for the walk. I arrived ten minutes later than usual, with a small bag of tomatoes and a much better opinion of getting lost. The route was not shorter, exactly, but it did come with directions and a snack.

title: The spare key
content: Found the spare key in the place I put it so I would not lose it. Future me has finally come through.
